candidate.rationale: The function returns alloc::format!("{:?}", v), which depends on the runtime Debug impl for T and on formatting/alloc internals that have no corresponding Verus spec-level abstraction in vstd. There is no existing public spec function that maps a value T: Debug to its formatted string, so any relation would either be unspecifiable or unsound (tightly coupling to implementation details or hidden state).
risks: The Debug implementation for T is not specified in Verus; asserting a concrete relation could be unsound if implementations differ or change.
Formatting may depend on platform/runtime details or cause panics; a spec that ignores these would be misleading.
Proposing a weak vacuous postcondition (e.g., about length or non-null) offers little verification value and may hide real behaviors.

candidate.rationale: The function produces a runtime-formatted String via alloc::format!("{:?}", v), which depends on the concrete Debug impl for T and on allocator/formatting internals (and private rt::Argument) that have no spec-level abstraction in vstd. There is no safe, stable, or meaningful spec-level mapping from T: Debug to its formatted string available; any attempted relation would either be implementation-dependent or vacuous.
risks: Tying a postcondition to the textual Debug output would be unsound because Debug formatting is not specified in Verus and can vary by implementation or platform.
Modeling formatting/alloc internals would tightly couple verification to hidden runtime details (rt::Argument, format internals), risking unsoundness and brittleness.
Weak/vacuous alternatives (e.g., non-empty, length bounds) offer little verification value and could mask real behaviors; they may also be false for some Debug implementations.
